mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate below 4.5% indicates accommodative monetary policy, which reduces discount rates for equity valuation and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly year-over-year CPI increase above 2.5% signals rising inflation, which may trigger Fed tightening and cause negative S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL YoY > 2.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in unemployment rate and increase in employment growth signals a strong labor market, boosting consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when PAYEMS increases and UNRATE decreases.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts above 1.2 million units (HOUST > 1200) during a post-recession recovery phase indicates improving consumer confidence and demand, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when HOUST > 1200 during the post-recession recovery regime.

mechanism_narrative: A rising industrial production index above 100 indicates strengthening supply-side activity, supporting corporate profits and leading to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 60-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when INDPRO > 100.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly decline in unemployment rate by more than 0.2 percentage points signals improving labor market conditions, which boosts consumer spending and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when UNRATE declines > 0.2pp.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in quarterly GDP growth and monthly retail sales growth indicates strong aggregate demand, driving corporate earnings and positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of periods when GDPC1 growth and RSAFS growth both increase.

mechanism_narrative: During high inflation periods (CPIAUCSL above 3.0%), the S&P 500 tends to decline over the next 5 trading days due to fears of aggressive monetary tightening by the Federal Reserve.
failure_condition: SPX 5-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods when CPIAUCSL > 3.0.
